A host without a working refs interface is refused, because an empty graph is the answer to "nothing depends on this", not to "I could not look".

tools.name: query_scene
tools.description: One entry point for the six read-side scene questions, selected by mode: overview for counts and a per-class histogram, filter for the node list narrowed by name, class for the node list narrowed by class name, property for one property read per node narrowed by value, selection for the selected nodes, and delta for what changed against a snapshot the caller captured earlier. Overview and delta answer with counts rather than a node list; every mode reports a warning instead of hiding a question the host could not answer. Delta compares the whole scene: name_filter and include_hidden do not narrow it, because a baseline captured without a filter is a statement about the whole scene and narrowing only the current side would report filtered-out nodes as removed.

name_filter.description: Case-insensitive node-name substring applied in every mode. At most 256 characters.

class_name.description: Class name to match in mode class. Required in that mode.

class_match.description: How class_name is compared in mode class: exact is case-insensitive equality, contains is a case-insensitive substring.

property_name.description: Property to read in mode property, or to compare in mode delta. Refused when it starts with an underscore.

property_value.description: In mode property, keep only the nodes whose property matches this value.

baseline.description: Required in mode delta. A node snapshot to compare against: an array of node names, or an array of objects carrying node_name, object_id, and optionally value or values. Pass the snapshot field returned when include_snapshot is true rather than the whole result object - overview and delta return an empty nodes list, which is not a baseline. Property comparison needs a baseline from property mode, whose nodes carry a value.

include_snapshot.description: Return a snapshot of the matched nodes so it can be passed back as the baseline of a later delta query.

limit.description: Maximum number of nodes to return or snapshot.

tools.intent: Answer one scene question: overview, filter, class, property, selection, or delta.

tools.name: undo_last
tools.description: Undo the most recent 3ds Max operations and verify each step. When to use: after a destructive or mutating tool call that needs to be reversed, including batch tools that touched several nodes. How to use: pass count equal to the number of host undo entries the reversed tool created - 1 for a single_call tool, one per node for a per_node tool (see docs/UNDO.md); a step the host accepted but that left the scene unchanged fails the call unless allow_no_op is true.

count.description: Number of host undo entries to reverse in this call.

allow_no_op.description: Report an undo that produced no scene change as a warning instead of a failure.

tools.intent: Reverse the most recent 3ds Max operations through the host undo stack.

tools.name: redo_last
tools.description: Redo the most recently undone 3ds Max operations and verify each step. When to use: after undo_last when the reversal was a mistake. How to use: the redo stack is cleared by any new edit, so call it immediately after the undo; a step with no scene change fails the call unless allow_no_op is true.

count.description: Number of host redo entries to replay in this call.

allow_no_op.description: Report a redo that produced no scene change as a warning instead of a failure.

tools.intent: Replay the most recently undone 3ds Max operations.

tools.name: get_undo_status
tools.description: Report which undo and redo entry points this 3ds Max host exposes, plus the current scene fingerprint. When to use: before relying on undo, or to compare the scene before and after a destructive call. How to use: the host exposes no history depth, so this reports capability only - an empty undo stack is discovered by calling undo_last.
tools.intent: Inspect undo and redo capability and the current scene fingerprint.

tools.name: move_object
tools.description: Move an object to a specified [x, y, z] location. The coordinates are written to the object's local translation channel (obj.location), which for an unparented object is its world position. parent_object cancels the parent transform into matrix_parent_inverse (parentinv = P^-1 @ W @ B^-1), so a child that was unparented when it was parented keeps world == matrix_basis: move_object([x, y, z]) on such a child moves it to the world position [x, y, z], not to [x, y, z] relative to its parent.

tools.name: assign_texture
tools.description: Assign a texture through an explicit Principled Shader, MaterialX, or Arnold contract.  Principled Shader uses its built-in texture toggle and path; supported image nodes update a string file parameter; supported MaterialX/Arnold surface nodes create and own one matching image-node connection per material input, then reuse it on repeated calls. Existing upstream nodes owned by another target are preserved. Texture files are bound to a regular-file identity and one digest pass (maximum 256 MiB, with elapsed time checked before and after each read). Windows holds a native write-denying lease through mutation, final readback, and undo exit. Linked files, stale/duplicate ownership, and unsupported string parameters fail without fallback wiring or partial graph mutation.

tools.name: render_rop
tools.description: Render a ROP/output driver and report written files, elapsed time, warnings/errors. Houdini defaults to an isolated job so UI and headless calls stay responsive. Plain calls return that render job_id directly; explicit MCP async metadata still returns a core job that must be resolved first. Pass background=false only for intentional foreground execution. Solaris LOP nodes return a typed redirect to USD export and Husk instead of being misclassified as ROPs.

background.description: Explicitly select isolated hython (true) or foreground (false) execution. When omitted, both interactive and headless Houdini use an isolated job. Headless isolation uses a job-owned temporary HIP snapshot without saving the source scene.

artifact_transaction.description: Optional staged publication contract for background renders with one primary multilayer EXR per integral frame. The worker discovers the exact ROP output parameter and creates same-directory staging names; the source HIP and final paths are never changed or overwritten.

tools.name: render_rop_chunked
tools.description: Render a ROP/output driver using per-frame chunked execution via the core ChunkedRunner. Each frame is a bounded step — UI stays interactive, cancellation is observable at checkpoints, and only partial outputs are reported on cancel. Supports launch/poll/cancel via the ``action`` param.

frame_range.description: Required for launch action. [start, end] or [start, end, increment].

job_id.description: Required for poll and cancel actions.

tools.name: get_render_job
tools.description: Read bounded status, output progress, elapsed time, and ETA for a background ROP render/cache/chain job. Set include_details only when full internal output and warning lists plus traceback data are required. The bounded summary includes warning_count and at most ten individually truncated recent_warnings. Accepts the returned 32-character hex job ID or its canonical dashed UUID spelling.

job_id.description: Adapter job ID in 32-character hex or canonical dashed UUID form.

include_details.description: Include full expected/output snapshots, written-file and warning lists, errors, and traceback data. The default response is bounded.

tools.name: finalize_render_outputs
tools.description: Publish one or more staged EXRs from a completed isolated render job. Each external validator receipt is bound to the job, frame, staging/final paths, byte count, mtime, SHA-256, and validator identity. Publication never replaces an existing final: Windows uses rename and POSIX uses hard-link plus unlink. Poll get_render_job for the transaction aggregate and set include_details=true for per-frame evidence.

tools.name: cancel_render_job
tools.description: Cancel a background ROP render/cache/chain job owned by the current adapter process. Accepts 32-character hex or canonical dashed UUID form. Repeated calls are safe.

job_id.description: Adapter job ID in 32-character hex or canonical dashed UUID form.

tools.name: search_assets
tools.description:
Search a directory tree for 3D asset files (FBX, OBJ, USD, MA, MB) matching
an optional name query. Returns a list of AssetDescriptor records that
maya-import-to-scene can consume directly. Each record includes the

are returned (up to max_results).

root_dir.description:
Absolute path to the root directory to search. Environment variables
and ~ are expanded.

query.description:
Optional case-insensitive substring to match against the asset file

Limit results to these formats. Defaults to all supported formats
when omitted.

max_results.description: Maximum number of AssetDescriptor records to return.

tools.name: resolve_asset
tools.description:
Resolve a single file path to an AssetDescriptor. Use this when you
already have a path and need the structured record required by
maya-import-to-scene. Returns an error if the file does not exist or
if the format is not supported.

path.description:
Absolute path to the asset file. Environment variables and ~ are
expanded. Must exist on disk.

evidence, automate Qt controls, and return stable refs while iterating with an agent. Not for general scene editing: use

tools.name: attach_project
tools.description: Attach a local Maya tool project to the live Maya Python session by adding its root (and optional src/ directory) to sys.path. Use this once before run_entrypoint/run_script. Set DCC_MCP_MAYA_DEV_ROOTS to restrict trusted roots in studio deployments.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the Python/Maya tool project root.

name.description: Optional session label; defaults to the directory name.

include_src.description: Also add project_root/src to sys.path when it exists.

make_active.description: Make this project the default target for later dev tools.

tools.name: reload_modules
tools.description: Purge or reload modules that belong to the attached development project. Default mode=purge removes matching modules from sys.modules so the next import sees edited files, which is usually safer than importlib.reload in long-lived Maya sessions.

project_name.description: Attached project label; defaults to the active project.

package_prefixes.description: Override package/module prefixes for this reload.

mode.description: purge removes modules from sys.modules; reload calls importlib.reload.

tools.name: run_entrypoint
tools.description: Run a callable from the attached development project inside Maya, with stdout/stderr/traceback captured into the result envelope. Use target="package.module:function" or module + callable.

module.description: Python module to import when target is not supplied.

project_name.description: Attached project label; defaults to the active project.

tools.name: run_script
tools.description: Run a project-local .py script with sys.argv, cwd, stdout/stderr, traceback, and elapsed time captured. The script must live under the attached project root.

script_path.description: Project-relative or absolute path to a .py file under the attached root.

tools.name: start_debugpy
tools.description: Try to start an optional debugpy listener inside the Maya process so Cursor or VS Code can attach breakpoints before MCP-triggered project code runs. If debugpy is absent, returns debugpy_missing with install guidance. Returns core-compatible debug-session metadata, suggested path mappings, and optional debugpy log location.

wait_for_client.description: Block until an IDE attaches. Usually keep false for agent workflows.

configure_python.description: Configure debugpy's Python executable from the Maya runtime when possible.

python_executable.description: Optional explicit Python/mayapy executable for debugpy.configure(python=...).

log_dir.description: Optional directory passed to debugpy.log_to; defaults to DCC_MCP_MAYA_DEBUGPY_LOG_DIR.

tools.name: capture_ui
tools.description: Capture the Maya main window or a named Qt widget as a base64 PNG. Use this for debugging custom tool windows and dock controls; use maya-render capture_viewport for viewport imagery.

object_name.description: Optional Qt objectName or windowTitle to capture instead of the whole main window.

tools.name: ui_snapshot
tools.description: Return a bounded tree of visible Maya Qt widgets using the core UI automation contract. Use before ui_find/ui_action when an agent needs UI structure.

object_name.description: Optional Qt objectName/windowTitle to use as the snapshot root.

tools.name: ui_find
tools.description: Find Maya Qt widgets by objectName, role/class, text, window title, tooltip, or fuzzy label. Returns stable session-scoped UiRef IDs for ui_action.

tools.description: Perform a bounded action on a unique Maya Qt control. Prefer passing control_id from ui_find/ui_snapshot; locator fields are accepted only when they resolve to exactly one enabled visible control.

text.description: Locator text, or value for set_text when value is omitted.

capture_screenshots.description: Capture before/after PNG artifact refs for action evidence.

tools.description: Return a stable JSON reference for a Maya node including long name, short name, type, UUID when available, existence, stale status, and scene metadata.

node.description: Maya node name, long DAG path, or unique short name.

tools.description: Resolve a previously returned Maya node reference by UUID, long name, or short name and report a structured stale-reference error if it no longer exists.

ref.description: NodeRef returned by make_node_ref or another Maya tool.

tools.name: run_check
tools.description: Development convenience wrapper: reload project modules, run an entrypoint, capture stdout/stderr/traceback, optionally capture a Maya UI screenshot, return artifact refs for large diagnostics, and publish bounded session events when core supports them. Use after editing project code to verify behavior inside the live Maya session.

tools.name: execute_mel
tools.description: Last-resort arbitrary MEL. Prefer search_skills → load_skill → typed tools. Inline MEL uses `code`; studio `.mel` files use `file_path` / `script_path` and are sourced with forward slashes.

code.description: Inline MEL to evaluate (required when file_path is omitted).

file_path.description: Path to a .mel file; sources via MEL `source` (native). Alias `script_path`.

tools.name: execute_python
tools.description: Bare-exec Python in Maya. Persistent globals (cmds / mel pre-bound). Off-main-thread calls are serialised through a bounded FIFO queue and marshaled to Maya's UI thread; QueueFullError on overflow. result_type ≠ NONE captures the trailing expression. Prefer search_skills / load_skill → typed tools when one fits; upload long scripts via write_module then call `import name; name.run()`.

code.description: Inline Python (required when file_path is omitted).

file_path.description: Absolute path to a .py file executed in __main__ with __file__ / this_root.

result_type.description: How to capture the last expression's value. NONE discards.

capture_output.description: Redirect sys.stdout / sys.stderr into the returned envelope.

inplace.description: Skip the automatic main-thread marshalling. By default, when the MCP handler runs off Maya's UI thread (hyper worker), user code is wrapped in maya.utils.executeInMainThreadWithResult so cmds.file / loadPlugin / scene-mutating cmds.* calls stay on the safe thread. Set inplace=true to opt out — only do this when you have already dispatched onto the main thread yourself or when the script touches no Maya state.

tools.name: write_module
tools.description: Inject a Python module into Maya's sys.modules from a source string. Same shape as maya-mcp-server's write_module. Use this to upload long scripts ONCE then call `execute_python(code='import name; name.run()')` many times — saves the agent prompt budget on repeated dispatch.

name.description: Dotted module name (each segment must be a valid Python identifier).

source.description: Python source for the module body.

overwrite.description: When true, re-exec the source against the existing module's __dict__.

tools.name: io
tools.description: Stdout / stderr capture + main-thread queue admin. Stream actions: install / uninstall / get / clear / status. Queue admin: `drain` cancels every QUEUED (not in-flight) main-thread job with WedgeDetectedError — use when Maya's UI thread is stuck and new MCP requests pile up. In-flight job is NOT cancellable (Maya is cooperative). affinity:any so drain works even when the pump is wedged.

drain.description: For action=get — drain the buffer (default) or peek without consuming.

reason.description: For action=drain — free-form label written to the cancelled futures' WedgeDetectedError envelope. Defaults to a generic message.

tools.name: pie_control
tools.description: Control the Play-In-Editor (PIE) session lifecycle: enter, pause, resume, or exit PIE. Does not depend on OS-level input — all PIE transitions use Unreal Engine's editor subsystem or in-process console commands.

action.description: PIE lifecycle action. "enter" starts a PIE session. "pause" freezes the simulation. "resume" continues after pause. "exit" or "stop" ends the PIE session and returns to editor mode.

tools.name: pie_inject_input
tools.description: Inject controlled keyboard or mouse input into the active PIE viewport using Unreal Engine's internal input subsystem. Never uses OS-level APIs like SendInput or pyautogui.

key.description: Key name (e.g. "W", "SpaceBar", "LeftMouseButton") for keyboard/ mouse button events. Uses Unreal Engine key names.

button.description: Mouse button name (used with mouse_button input_type).

position_x.description: Optional horizontal position for mouse_button, normalized across the active Unreal window. Must be paired with position_y.

position_y.description: Optional vertical position for mouse_button, normalized across the active Unreal window. Must be paired with position_x.

delta_x.description: Horizontal possessed-controller look delta (used with mouse_move). Positive values turn right.

delta_y.description: Vertical possessed-controller look delta (used with mouse_move). Positive values look down.

duration.description: Hold duration in seconds for key_tap (0.0 = instant).

tools.name: pie_capture_screenshot
tools.description: Request an asynchronous PNG screenshot of the active Unreal viewport. The result reports capture_pending until the specified file appears. Falls back to HighResShot when AutomationLibrary is unavailable.

filepath.description: Absolute path for the output PNG file. Directory is created if missing. Defaults to "<ProjectSaved>/Screenshots/pie_<timestamp>.png".

resolution_x.description: Viewport width override (0 = current viewport size).

resolution_y.description: Viewport height override (0 = current viewport size).

tools.name: pie_get_screenshot_job
tools.description: Poll an adapter-owned screenshot job and report completed only after the requested PNG exists on disk with a non-zero size.

tools.name: pie_snapshot_log
tools.description: Read a bounded snapshot from the Unreal Engine Output Log. The filter matches log categories only; use message_contains for message text. Supports time windows, a continuation cursor, and optional deduplication.

max_lines.description: Maximum number of log lines to return.

filter.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter applied to the log category only. Empty string returns all matching lines.

message_contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter on message text.

include_verbosity.description: Whether to include verbosity tags (Error, Warning, Log) in output.

since_timestamp.description: Inclusive ISO-8601 lower time bound for timestamped log lines.

until_timestamp.description: Inclusive ISO-8601 upper time bound for timestamped log lines.

since_line.description: Zero-based physical log line offset to start reading from.

cursor.description: Numeric continuation cursor returned by a file-backed snapshot; tail-only unreal.log snapshots do not support continuation.

dedupe.description: Collapse repeated category/message pairs and report occurrence_counts.

tools.name: pie_get_status
tools.description: Query the current PIE session state (playing/paused/stopped) and collect performance counters: FPS, frame time, game thread time, render thread time, GPU time, and memory usage where available.

tools.name: pie_run_test
tools.description: Queue a native Unreal Automation Test run by filter string. Returns a job_id that can be polled via pie_poll_test and cancelled via pie_cancel_job. The test runs asynchronously; use pie_snapshot_log or pie_poll_test to monitor progress.

filter.description: Automation test name or filter string, e.g. "DccMcp.Smoke" or "Project.Functional.Tests".

tools.name: pie_poll_test
tools.description: Poll the status and results of a previously queued Automation Test job. Returns the job's current state (queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled) and, when complete, the test outcome details.

tools.name: pie_cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a previously queued Automation Test or PIE job. Marks the job as cancelled in the job registry. Does not force-kill the Unreal process.

tools.name: playtest_execute_action
tools.description: Execute one bounded semantic gameplay action in the active PIE world. Navigation follows Unreal navigation and never teleports the player. Movement can require a measured displacement instead of treating input delivery as success. Relative movement proof is direction- and duration- bounded; displacement values use Unreal centimeters.

direction.description: Camera-relative gameplay direction used only by move_relative.

target_exclude_class_contains.description: Reject matching target classes even when another selector matches.

target_include_hidden.description: Allow targeting actors hidden in game. Disabled by default.

target_location.description: Explicit world-space point used by navigate_to_location or face_location.

duration.description: Hold duration for finite gameplay input, including move_relative.

require_line_of_sight.description: Reject targeted attacks before input when the player controller has no line of sight.

expect_movement.description: Require a measured player displacement for movement actions. Defaults to true for move_relative and false for navigation, where reaching the requested target is already an observed effect.

min_displacement.description: Minimum measured player displacement in Unreal centimeters required when movement is expected.

call_examples.note: Require an observed movement effect instead of input acceptance alone.

tools.name: playtest_poll_action
tools.description: Poll a semantic playtest action and return its structured transition. event_name.description: Name of the UMG event to bind.

function_name.description: Name of the Blueprint function to bind. Will be created if it does not exist.

create_function.description: Whether to auto-create the Blueprint function if it does not exist.

tools.name: create_umg_animation
tools.description: Create a new UMG WidgetAnimation track on a widget within a Widget Blueprint. The animation is stored as a named timeline that can receive keyframes for position, opacity, color, scale, rotation, visibility, or shear properties.

widget_blueprint_path.description: Asset path of the Widget Blueprint to add the animation to.

animation_name.description: Unique name for the new WidgetAnimation.

target_widget_name.description: Name of the widget to animate.

num_loops_to_play.description: Number of loops (-1 for infinite, only when loop is true).

call_examples.note: Create a fade-in animation for the title
Create a looping pulse animation for Start button

tools.name: add_animation_keyframe
tools.description: Add a keyframe to an existing UMG WidgetAnimation track. Supports keying position (RenderTransform.Translation), opacity (RenderOpacity), color (ColorAndOpacity), scale (RenderTransform.Scale), rotation (RenderTransform.Angle), visibility, and shear (RenderTransform.Shear).

widget_blueprint_path.description: Asset path of the Widget Blueprint containing the animation.

animation_name.description: Name of the WidgetAnimation to add the keyframe to.

time.description: Time in seconds for this keyframe.

value.description: Keyframe value — type depends on the property.

oneOf.description: Opacity as a float 0.0-1.0, or rotation as degrees.
Color as {r, g, b, a} with values 0.0-1.0.

call_examples.note: Key opacity to 0 at time 0
Key opacity to 1 at time 0.5 — fade in complete

tools.name: compile_widget_blueprint
tools.description: Compile a Widget Blueprint and return any compilation errors or warnings. Use this after making a batch of widget changes to validate the blueprint state.

widget_blueprint_path.description: Asset path of the Widget Blueprint to compile.

call_examples.note: Compile the main menu widget blueprint

tools.name: list_widget_hierarchy
tools.description: Read the full widget tree hierarchy from a Widget Blueprint, returning the widget type, name, parent, and children for each widget in the tree.

widget_blueprint_path.description: Asset path of the Widget Blueprint to inspect.

root_widget_name.description: Optional root widget name. Defaults to the blueprint's root widget.

max_depth.description: Maximum depth to traverse. Defaults to 10.

call_examples.note: List full widget hierarchy of the main menu
Inspect the top 3 levels under CanvasPanel_0
